newsitem.title: SWEDEN: ASTRA SAYS PRILOSEC COULD GAIN IN U.S.
newsitem.headline: ASTRA SAYS PRILOSEC COULD GAIN IN U.S.

text.p: Swedish drugs group Astra said on Friday its blockbuster anti-ulcer agent Losec, called Prilosec in the U.S., has potential to achieve a 45 percent market share in the U.S. from its current 35 percent.
Astra also said its research and development (R&D) costs would increase faster than sales this year but that its increased marketing efforts would give both short-term and long-term benefits.

"We have reached 50 percent market share in Europe (for Losec) and around 35 percent in the U.S... We might not be able to reach 50 percent in the U.S. but we might be able to take another 10 percent," said Astra Chief Executive Hakan Mogren.
If Prilosec has a chance of reaching this level it needs to do it fast, within a couple of years, Mogren told a news conference in connection with the group releasing earnings.

Mogren said the market share estimates were based on current prices and that it was hard to estimate how the value of the U.S. ulcer agent market would develop as rival Glaxo's patent for Zantac had expired.
Additionally, Astra said it saw R&D costs growing quicker than sales in 1997.
"This year we will have a faster increase (of R&D) than sales," Astra's financial director Ake Stavling said.
But in the long-term Astra sees R&D costs increasing at the same rate as sales.
In the first six months of the year, the group's R&D costs rose 22 percent to 3.99 billion crowns. At fixed foreign exchange rates R&D costs rose 16 percent.
Regarding marketing, Mogren said that although the company's focus on marketing is a long-term strategy, it will also have shortterm benefits.
"In the shortterm we will have return on this (marketing) with existing products but in the longer term the increased sales force that will take care of new products," Mogren said.
He did not see the fall in second quarter operating margin in as serious.
"If we had wanted to show profit in the shortterm it would not have been a problem but now we choose to take these costs instead," Mogren said.
Astra's second quarter operating margin fell to 29.9 percent from 32 percent in the same quarter a year earlier while costs rose 20 percent to 7.95 billion crowns.

Astra reported a 13 percent rise in six-month sales to 21.47 billion crowns ($2.7 billion) and a four percent lift in pre-tax profits to 7.01 billion crowns, which was lower than the consensus market forecast of 7.18 billion.
